caption: How hi agent works. You hand a task to hi agent. It checks out your last commit into a new worktree on its own branch, starts a box on it, and starts the proxy, the only part that holds the agent's sign-in. Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes works in the box without permission prompts, with a placeholder token. When the agent stops, hi writes one report, the same shape for every agent: what it said, whether the tests pass, the changed files, tokens, and cost. You review the branch and keep it with git merge.

items.title: hi-box/myproject-1
items.does: The agent's commits wait here for you. Uncommitted changes stay out.

items.title: myproject-1
items.does: Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes, without permission prompts. Its token is a placeholder.

items.title: myproject-1-proxy
items.does: Puts your real token on calls to the model's API, and lets through only allowed hosts.

items.title: hi agent wait myproject-1
items.does: What it said, whether the tests pass, changed files, tokens, and cost; `--json` for scripts.

items.title: hi box diff myproject-1
items.does: `git merge hi-box/myproject-1` keeps the work; `hi box rm` cleans up. `best-of` runs several and ranks them.

key.text: Where hi and the agent's sign-in live; the agent gets neither.
A fresh checkout on its own branch, so nothing changes in your folder.
Where the agent works without prompts: it can't read your keys or leave through anything but the proxy.
The only part with your real token; it adds it on the way to the model's API.
The same for every agent, so a script or another agent can read it.
